subject: Materials Science
title: Fracture Toughness: Resisting Cracks
description: A 60-second lesson on Fracture Toughness: Resisting Cracks.

hook.text: A ceramic knife is sharp but shatters if dropped. A steel knife dulls but never breaks. Why?

buildup.text: Fracture toughness (K_IC) measures resistance to crack propagation — how hard it is to grow a crack.

discovery.text: Tough materials absorb energy by plastic deformation at the crack tip — blunting it before it can grow.

twist.text: Strength and toughness often oppose each other — the hardest steels are often the most brittle.

climax.text: Aircraft are designed with damage tolerance — cracks must grow slowly enough to be found before failure.

punchline.text: Toughness isn't about being strong — it's about resisting catastrophe.

quiz.question: What does fracture toughness measure?
options: The hardness of a material's surface
